c.tagline: South India's Dravidian capital of temples, filter coffee, and the world's second-longest urban beach.

taxi.fareNote: Auto-rickshaws rarely use the meter and require firm negotiation before boarding; app cabs (Uber/Ola) and prepaid airport counters give the most predictable, honest fares.

emergency.note: 112 is India's single all-in-one emergency number connecting to police, fire, and ambulance; 100 reaches police directly and 108 is the dedicated ambulance line.

hood_landmark.Nungambakkam: Khader Nawaz Khan Road, Nungambakkam, Chennai

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing at markets and on the beach; touts and taxi/auto overcharging

hood_desc: The historic core along the Marina Beach seafront around Triplicane, home to the Parthasarathy Temple, the Ice House, and cheap lodges; best for first-timers who want to be near the water, temples, and budget eats.

Chennai's frenetic shopping district packed with silk-saree emporiums, jewellery showrooms, and Ranganathan Street's crowds; suits travelers who want retail therapy and are happy amid noise and bustle.

The cultural and spiritual heart around the Kapaleeshwarar Temple, San Thome Basilica, and December music-season sabhas; suits travelers wanting classical arts, heritage, and traditional Tamil Brahmin life.

A leafy, upmarket central area of hotels, consulates, restaurants, and Khader Nawaz Khan Road's boutiques; a convenient, slightly quieter base for business travelers and those wanting dining within walking distance.

A relaxed, affluent southern district stretching toward the East Coast Road (ECR) with cafes, the Theosophical Society gardens, and easy access to Elliot's Beach; suits families and those wanting calm and greenery.
lodging: Keys Prima by Lemon Tree Hotels, Katti-Ma

water.note: Tap water is not safe for visitors; use bottled or filtered water, including for brushing teeth.

transit.hours: Chennai Metro runs roughly 4:30 AM to 11:00 PM; suburban and MRTS local trains run from around 4:00 AM to 11:00 PM; city buses run late but night frequency is sparse.
transit.note: Chennai Metro (CMRL) covers key corridors and the airport, complemented by an extensive suburban rail network, the MRTS elevated line, and MTC city buses; auto-rickshaws and app cabs fill the gaps.
transit.pay: Metro uses tokens, QR tickets via app, and the rechargeable Singara Chennai / travel smart card; suburban rail and MTC buses take cash and, increasingly, UPI/QR payments. As of 2026 there is no single card covering all modes.

bus: SETC/state intercity buses from CMBT Koyambedu to other Tamil Nadu and South Indian cities
train: Long-distance rail from Chennai Central and Chennai Egmore stations

transit.m: Chennai Metro Blue Line from Airport station to city center (~40 min)
Suburban rail from Tirusulam station (adjacent to airport) to Beach/Tambaram
Prepaid taxi or app cab to city center (30-45 min)

tip.r: Not expected but appreciated; rounding up or leaving 5-10% at restaurants and small tips for hotel staff and drivers is customary for good service.

food.name: Idli with sambar and chutney
food.desc: Steamed fermented rice-and-lentil cakes, feather-light, dunked in sambar and coconut chutney with a spoonful of ghee and podi.

places.name: Murugan Idli Shop
places.note: Chennai's most famous idli address; served on banana leaf with a legendary coconut chutney.

places.name: Ratna Cafe
places.note: Running since 1948 and known citywide for drowning its idlis in sambar.

places.name: Hotel Saravana Bhavan
places.note: The vegetarian chain that took Tamil tiffin worldwide; consistent from dawn onwards.

food.name: Ghee roast dosa
food.desc: A paper-thin fermented crepe griddled crisp with ghee, rolled into a cone and served with sambar and three chutneys.

places.name: Sangeetha Veg Restaurant
places.note: Dependable all-day tiffin chain; locals rate its dosas and evening snacks highly.

places.name: Rayar's Mess
places.note: Tiny, decades-old mess with limited hours and a devoted following for old-style tiffin.

places.name: Adyar Ananda Bhavan
places.note: Sweet-shop-and-tiffin institution, easy to find anywhere in the city.

food.name: Chettinad chicken
food.desc: Fiery Chettinad masala of star anise, stone flower and black pepper clinging to chicken, eaten with parotta or rice.

places.name: Anjappar Chettinad Restaurant
places.note: The Chettinad chain that started in Chennai; the standard reference for the cuisine.

places.name: Ponnusamy Hotel
places.note: Old-school non-veg institution since 1953, strong on pepper chicken and country dishes.

places.name: Karaikudi Restaurant
places.note: Named for the Chettinad heartland; well regarded for authentic regional spicing.

food.name: Kothu parotta
food.desc: Flaky parotta shredded on a hot griddle with egg, salna and minced meat, chopped to a rhythmic clang you can hear down the street.

places.name: Dindigul Thalappakatti
places.note: Best known for biryani but its kothu parotta and salna are a late-night Chennai staple.

places.name: Sri Velu Military Hotel
places.note: Classic Chennai military hotel; unpolished, cheap and serious about meat dishes.

places.name: Buhari Hotel
places.note: Historic Chennai restaurant credited with inventing chicken 65; long-running late-night kitchen.

food.name: Sundal
food.desc: Boiled chickpeas or black-eyed peas tossed with coconut, mustard seed and curry leaf, sold in paper cones on the beach.

places.name: Marina Beach promenade
places.note: Sundal and bajji carts work the sand every evening; the definitive Chennai beach snack.

places.name: Elliot's Beach
places.note: Calmer southern beach with the same vendors and a stronger local crowd.

places.name: Mylapore Mada Streets
places.note: Stalls around the Kapaleeshwarar temple tank, especially busy during festivals.

food.name: Ambur-style biryani
food.desc: Short-grain seeraga samba rice cooked with mutton, chilli and mint - lighter and tangier than Hyderabadi, served with brinjal dalcha.

places.name: Dindigul Thalappakatti
places.note: The seeraga samba mutton biryani that made a Dindigul shop into a Chennai obsession.

places.name: Ambur Star Briyani
places.note: Brings the Ambur recipe to the city; served with the traditional onion raita and dalcha.

places.name: Junior Kuppanna
places.note: Kongunadu kitchen popular for mutton biryani and non-veg thalis.

food.name: Filter coffee
food.desc: Chicory-blended coffee brewed by drip, whipped with hot milk and poured between tumbler and davara until it foams.

places.name: Kumbakonam Degree Coffee
places.note: Named for the degree of milk purity; a reliable strong, sweet, foamy pour.

places.name: Rayar's Mess
places.note: Old Mylapore mess where the coffee is as much the draw as the tiffin.

places.name: Amethyst Cafe
places.note: Garden cafe in a colonial bungalow; a calm place for filter coffee and cake.

food.name: Rose milk
food.desc: Chilled milk with rose syrup and sometimes sabja seeds - Chennai's answer to the afternoon heat, drunk standing at a stall.

places.name: Kalathi Rose Milk
places.note: A Mylapore landmark for decades; the rose milk locals queue for after temple visits.

places.name: Mylapore Mada Streets
places.note: Sarbath stalls around the temple selling nannari and rose coolers all afternoon.

places.name: Marina Beach promenade
places.note: Juice and sarbath carts along the sand for an evening cooler by the sea.

landmarks: Marina Beach
One of the longest urban beaches in the world, its wide golden sands, lighthouse, and lively promenade make it Chennai's most iconic gathering spot.
Kapaleeshwarar Temple
A vividly painted, towering Dravidian gopuram in Mylapore, this ancient Shiva temple is the beating cultural heart of old Chennai.
Santhome Basilica
A striking neo-Gothic white church built over the tomb of St. Thomas the Apostle, its spires make a dramatic silhouette against the sea.
Fort St. George
The first English fortress in India, this 17th-century bastion houses colonial-era buildings and a fascinating museum of Chennai's founding history.
Valluvar Kottam
A soaring 39-meter stone chariot-shaped monument honoring the Tamil poet Thiruvalluvar, instantly recognizable on Chennai's skyline.
Government Museum, Egmore
One of India's oldest museums, its elegant Indo-Saracenic buildings house an outstanding collection of Chola bronzes and antiquities.
Vivekananda House
A distinctive domed seaside Ice House where Swami Vivekananda once stayed, now a memorial with striking colonial architecture.
Parthasarathy Temple
One of the oldest temples in Chennai, this ornately carved Vaishnavite shrine in Triplicane dates back over a thousand years.
Ashtalakshmi Temple
A striking multi-tiered temple perched right on the Besant Nagar coastline, offering a beautifully photogenic blend of architecture and sea.
Guindy National Park
A rare urban national park with deer, blackbuck, and lush greenery, offering a surprising natural escape within Chennai's city limits.

train.note: No international trains - the old Indo-Ceylon boat-train link to Sri Lanka has not run since 1964. Chennai Central (Puratchi Thalaivar Dr. M.G. Ramachandran Central) handles northbound long-distance trains and Chennai Egmore the southern Tamil Nadu routes. Book on IRCTC from 60 days out; the Vande Bharat to Bengaluru and Mysuru and the overnight trains to Kerala fill quickly.

bus.note: No international coaches. Long-distance buses use the huge Kilambakkam terminal in the south-west, which replaced Koyambedu for most intercity routes in 2024 - allow extra time to reach it. The state operator TNSTC and SETC run to Bengaluru, Madurai, Puducherry and Kerala, with private sleeper coaches bookable through redBus (https://www.redbus.in/).

intl.to: Port Blair, Andaman & Nicobar Islands (India) - 3-4 day passenger ship
intl.op: Shipping Corporation of India / A&N Administration — tickets at the Chennai Port shipping office, no online booking

ferry.note: Chennai has no international passenger ferry; the long-discussed Chennai-Colombo and Tuticorin-Jaffna links have never settled into a regular service. The Andaman Islands ship sails from Chennai Port a few times a month, takes three to four days and is far slower and cheaper than flying - tickets are sold in person and berths are limited. Bookings open roughly a month before sailing.

half.name: Mahabalipuram (Mamallapuram)
half.blurb: A UNESCO seaside town of 7th-century rock-cut shore temples and monolithic rathas carved directly from granite outcrops.

half.name: Kanchipuram
half.blurb: One of Hinduism's seven sacred cities, packed with ancient temple complexes and famous for its handwoven silk sarees.

full.name: Puducherry (Pondicherry)
full.blurb: A former French colonial enclave with a tidy seafront promenade, mustard-and-white villas and the Auroville township nearby.

full.name: Vellore
full.blurb: Home to a moated 16th-century stone fort and the gold-plated Sripuram Golden Temple set amid landscaped hills.

full.name: Tirupati
full.blurb: One of the world's most-visited pilgrimage sites, centered on the hilltop Venkateswara Temple atop the Tirumala hills.
